title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables: Geometric Behavior & Consistency Criteria
description: Understand the general form of a pair of linear equations in two variables. Master the three geometric configurations (intersecting, parallel, coincident) and their algebraic criteria based on ratio comparisons of coefficients.
key_concepts: Standard Form: a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0
Geometric Meaning: Each linear equation represents a straight line in the plane
Case 1 (Intersecting Lines): a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ ⇒ Unique Solution (Consistent)
Case 2 (Coincident Lines): a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂ ⇒ Infinitely Many Solutions (Consistent & Dependent)
Case 3 (Parallel Lines): a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ ⇒ No Solution (Inconsistent)
Graphical Solution Method: Finding intersection coordinates (x, y)
subtopics: Derivation and proof of ratio criteria
Formulating equations from physical scenarios (Akhila in fair)
Distinguishing consistent vs inconsistent systems

worked_examples.problem: Check graphically whether the pair of equations x + 3y = 6 and 2x - 3y = 12 is consistent. If so, solve them graphically.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Equation (1): x + 3y = 6 ⇒ y = (6 - x)/3
Equation (2): 2x - 3y = 12 ⇒ y = (2x - 12)/3
To find: Consistency and graphical solution.

Step 1: Check consistency by ratio comparison:
a₁ = 1, b₁ = 3, c₁ = -6
a₂ = 2, b₂ = -3, c₂ = -12
a₁/a₂ = 1/2
b₁/b₂ = 3/(-3) = -1
Since a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂ (1/2 ≠ -1), the lines intersect at a unique point. System is Consistent.

Step 2: Table of values for Equation (1): x + 3y = 6
x = 0 ⇒ y = 2  → Point (0, 2)
x = 6 ⇒ y = 0  → Point (6, 0)
x = 3 ⇒ y = 1  → Point (3, 1)

Step 3: Table of values for Equation (2): 2x - 3y = 12
x = 0 ⇒ y = -4 → Point (0, -4)
x = 6 ⇒ y = 0  → Point (6, 0)
x = 3 ⇒ y = -2 → Point (3, -2)

Step 4: Plotting and Point of Intersection:
Both lines pass through the common point (6, 0).
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check at (6, 0):
Eq 1: 6 + 3(0) = 6 (True)
Eq 2: 2(6) - 3(0) = 12 (True)
Boxed Answer: [ The pair of equations is consistent. The unique solution is x = 6, y = 0 ].
concept_questions: What is the physical meaning of the intersection point of two lines?
If a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂, why does that imply the slopes of the lines are equal?
What is the difference between an independent system and a dependent system?

common_misconceptions: Forgetting to write equations in standard form (moving c to LHS) before comparing ratios: If c₁ is on LHS and c₂ is on RHS, the sign of c₁/c₂ will be inverted!
Believing that parallel lines have a solution at infinity: In standard Euclidean geometry, parallel lines have strictly NO solution.

title: Algebraic Resolution Foundations: Masterclass in Substitution & Elimination Methods
description: Master the two primary algebraic methods for solving systems of linear equations: Method of Substitution and Method of Elimination. Understand when one method is algebraically superior to the other.
key_concepts: Substitution Method Protocol: Express one variable in terms of the other, substitute into the second equation, solve linear equation in 1 variable
Elimination Method Protocol: Equalize coefficients of one variable by LCM multiplication, add or subtract equations to eliminate, solve and back-substitute
Detecting Inconsistency Algebraically: Arriving at a false statement (e.g. 0 = 8) ⇒ No solution
Detecting Dependent Systems Algebraically: Arriving at a true identity (e.g. 0 = 0) ⇒ Infinitely many solutions
Fractional and Radical Linear Equations
subtopics: Substitution step-by-step algorithm
Elimination step-by-step algorithm
Worked Examples 7, 8, 9, 10 from NCERT
Handling systems with decimal coefficients and square roots

worked_examples.problem: Example 7 (NCERT): Solve the following pair of equations by substitution method: 7x - 15y = 2 ... (1), and x + 2y = 3 ... (2).
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
7x - 15y = 2 ... (1)
x + 2y = 3 ... (2)
To find: Values of x and y using Substitution Method.

Step 1: Express x in terms of y from Equation (2) (since coefficient of x is 1):
x = 3 - 2y ... (3)

Step 2: Substitute expression (3) into Equation (1):
7(3 - 2y) - 15y = 2
21 - 14y - 15y = 2
21 - 29y = 2
-29y = 2 - 21
-29y = -19
y = 19/29.

Step 3: Substitute y = 19/29 into Equation (3) to find x:
x = 3 - 2(19/29) = 3 - 38/29 = (87 - 38)/29 = 49/29.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check in Eq (1):
7(49/29) - 15(19/29) = (343 - 285)/29 = 58/29 = 2. (Verified!)
Check in Eq (2):
49/29 + 2(19/29) = (49 + 38)/29 = 87/29 = 3. (Verified!)
Boxed Answer: [ x = 49/29, y = 19/29 ].
concept_questions: Why did we choose to express x in terms of y from Equation (2) rather than Equation (1)?
What would happen if you substituted equation (3) back into equation (2) instead of equation (1)?

worked_examples.problem: Example 9 (NCERT): Solve 2x + 3y = 8 ... (1) and 4x + 6y = 7 ... (2) by elimination method.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
2x + 3y = 8 ... (1)
4x + 6y = 7 ... (2)

Step 1: Multiply Equation (1) by 2 to equalize coefficients of x:
2 × (2x + 3y = 8) ⇒ 4x + 6y = 16 ... (3)

Step 2: Subtract Equation (2) from Equation (3):
(4x + 6y) - (4x + 6y) = 16 - 7
0 = 9.

Step 3: Analysis of result:
The statement 0 = 9 is a mathematical contradiction (false statement).
Therefore, the given pair of equations has no common solution.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Ratio comparison:
a₁/a₂ = 2/4 = 1/2
b₁/b₂ = 3/6 = 1/2
c₁/c₂ = 8/7
a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂ ⇒ Lines are parallel!
Boxed Answer: [ The pair of equations has no solution (inconsistent system) ].
concept_questions: What does arriving at 0 = 9 tell you geometrically about the two lines?
What algebraic result would you get if the lines were coincident?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.1 Q1 (i): 10 students of Class X took part in a Mathematics quiz. If the number of girls is 4 more than the number of boys, find the number of boys and girls who took part in the quiz graphically.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Total students = 10. Girls = Boys + 4.
Let number of girls = x, number of boys = y.
Equation (1): x + y = 10
Equation (2): x - y = 4 (or x = y + 4)

Table for x + y = 10:
x = 5, y = 5; x = 7, y = 3; x = 6, y = 4.

Table for x - y = 4:
x = 4, y = 0; x = 7, y = 3; x = 6, y = 2.

Intersection: Both lines intersect at (7, 3).
[ROUGH_WORK]
Total = 7 + 3 = 10
Difference = 7 - 3 = 4
Boxed Answer: [ Number of girls = 7, Number of boys = 3 ].
concept_questions: How can you verify this result algebraically in 10 seconds?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.1 Q1 (ii): 5 pencils and 7 pens together cost ₹ 50, whereas 7 pencils and 5 pens together cost ₹ 46. Find the cost of one pencil and that of one pen graphically.
worked_examples.solution:
Let cost of 1 pencil = ₹ x, cost of 1 pen = ₹ y.
Equation (1): 5x + 7y = 50
Equation (2): 7x + 5y = 46

Points for Eq (1): 5x + 7y = 50 ⇒ y = (50 - 5x)/7
x = 3 ⇒ y = 35/7 = 5 → (3, 5)
x = 10 ⇒ y = 0 → (10, 0)
x = -4 ⇒ y = 70/7 = 10 → (-4, 10)

Points for Eq (2): 7x + 5y = 46 ⇒ y = (46 - 7x)/5
x = 3 ⇒ y = (46 - 21)/5 = 25/5 = 5 → (3, 5)
x = 8 ⇒ y = (46 - 56)/5 = -10/5 = -2 → (8, -2)

Intersection: The lines intersect at (3, 5).
[ROUGH_WORK]
5(3) + 7(5) = 15 + 35 = 50
7(3) + 5(5) = 21 + 25 = 46
Boxed Answer: [ Cost of one pencil = ₹ 3, Cost of one pen = ₹ 5 ].
concept_questions: Why is choosing integer points for the table so helpful when plotting graphs?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.1 Q5: Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden, whose length is 4 m more than its width, is 36 m. Find the dimensions of the garden.
worked_examples.solution:
Let length of garden = x metres, width of garden = y metres.
Given: Length is 4 m more than width ⇒ x = y + 4 ⇒ x - y = 4 ... (1)
Half perimeter = 36 m ⇒ (2x + 2y)/2 = 36 ⇒ x + y = 36 ... (2)

Adding (1) and (2):
(x - y) + (x + y) = 4 + 36
2x = 40 ⇒ x = 20 m.
Substitute x = 20 into (2):
20 + y = 36 ⇒ y = 16 m.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Perimeter = 2(20 + 16) = 2(36) = 72 m.
Half perimeter = 36 m.
Length - Width = 20 - 16 = 4 m.
Boxed Answer: [ Length = 20 m, Width = 16 m ].
concept_questions: Why does the half perimeter formula simplify to x + y?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.1 Q7: Draw the graphs of the equations x - y + 1 = 0 and 3x + 2y - 12 = 0. Determine the coordinates of the vertices of the triangle formed by these lines and the x-axis, and shade the triangular region.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Line 1: x - y + 1 = 0 ⇒ y = x + 1
Line 2: 3x + 2y - 12 = 0 ⇒ 2y = 12 - 3x ⇒ y = (12 - 3x)/2

Step 1: Find points for Line 1 (x - y + 1 = 0):
When x = 0, y = 1 → (0, 1)
When y = 0, x = -1 → (-1, 0) [x-intercept]
When x = 2, y = 3 → (2, 3)

Step 2: Find points for Line 2 (3x + 2y - 12 = 0):
When x = 0, y = 6 → (0, 6)
When y = 0, 3x = 12 ⇒ x = 4 → (4, 0) [x-intercept]
When x = 2, y = (12 - 6)/2 = 3 → (2, 3)

Step 3: Point of intersection of Line 1 and Line 2:
Both lines pass through (2, 3). So vertex A = (2, 3).

Step 4: Intersections with x-axis (y = 0):
Line 1 intersects x-axis at B(-1, 0).
Line 2 intersects x-axis at C(4, 0).

Step 5: Vertices of the triangle formed by lines and the x-axis:
A(2, 3), B(-1, 0), C(4, 0).

Step 6: Area of the shaded triangle:
Base = distance BC along x-axis = 4 - (-1) = 5 units.
Height = y-coordinate of vertex A = 3 units.
Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 5 × 3 = 15/2 = 7.5 sq units.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Distance BC = |4 - (-1)| = 5
Altitude h = 3 - 0 = 3
Area = 0.5 * 5 * 3 = 7.5
Boxed Answer: [ Vertices are A(2, 3), B(-1, 0), and C(4, 0). Shaded Area = 7.5 square units ].
concept_questions: What would be the vertices if the question asked for the triangle formed with the y-axis instead?
How do you determine the height of the triangle from the coordinates of the apex?

description: Exhaustive resolution of NCERT Exercise 3.2 Question 1 (all 6 parts including radical and decimal equations), Question 2 (finding m in y = mx + 3), and Question 3 (all 6 authentic word problems: numbers difference, supplementary angles, cricket bats, taxi charges, fractions, and Jacob's age).

Ex 3.2 Q3(iv): Fixed taxi charge + charge per km (10 km costs ₹ 105, 15 km costs ₹ 155; find cost for 25 km)

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.2 Q1 (iv): Solve 0.2x + 0.3y = 1.3 and 0.4x + 0.5y = 2.3 by the substitution method.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
0.2x + 0.3y = 1.3 ... (1)
0.4x + 0.5y = 2.3 ... (2)

Step 1: Multiply both equations by 10 to eliminate decimals:
2x + 3y = 13 ... (3)
4x + 5y = 23 ... (4)

Step 2: Express x in terms of y from (3):
2x = 13 - 3y ⇒ x = (13 - 3y)/2 ... (5)

Step 3: Substitute (5) into (4):
4[(13 - 3y)/2] + 5y = 23
2(13 - 3y) + 5y = 23
26 - 6y + 5y = 23
26 - y = 23 ⇒ y = 3.

Step 4: Substitute y = 3 into (5):
x = (13 - 3(3))/2 = (13 - 9)/2 = 4/2 = 2.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check in original:
0.2(2) + 0.3(3) = 0.4 + 0.9 = 1.3 (True)
0.4(2) + 0.5(3) = 0.8 + 1.5 = 2.3 (True)
Boxed Answer: [ x = 2, y = 3 ].
concept_questions: Why is multiplying by 10 allowed in an equation?
Would you get the exact same answer if you solved without clearing decimals?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.2 Q1 (v): Solve √2 x + √3 y = 0 and √3 x - √8 y = 0 by the substitution method.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
√2 x + √3 y = 0 ... (1)
√3 x - √8 y = 0 ... (2)

Step 1: From Equation (1), express x in terms of y:
√2 x = -√3 y ⇒ x = (-√3 / √2) y ... (3)

Step 2: Substitute (3) into Equation (2):
√3 [ (-√3 / √2) y ] - √8 y = 0
(-3 / √2) y - √8 y = 0
y [ (-3 / √2) - √8 ] = 0
Notice that the bracketed term is strictly non-zero: (-3 / √2 - 2√2) = -7/√2 ≠ 0.
Therefore: y = 0.

Step 3: Substitute y = 0 into (3):
x = (-√3 / √2)(0) = 0.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Since both equations have constant term c = 0, both lines pass through origin (0, 0).
Boxed Answer: [ x = 0, y = 0 ].

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.2 Q2: Solve 2x + 3y = 11 and 2x - 4y = -24 and hence find the value of 'm' for which y = mx + 3.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
2x + 3y = 11 ... (1)
2x - 4y = -24 ... (2)
Target: Find x, y, and then m in y = mx + 3.

Step 1: From (1), 2x = 11 - 3y ⇒ x = (11 - 3y)/2

Step 2: Substitute into (2):
2[(11 - 3y)/2] - 4y = -24
(11 - 3y) - 4y = -24
11 - 7y = -24
-7y = -35 ⇒ y = 5.

Step 3: Find x:
x = (11 - 3(5))/2 = (11 - 15)/2 = -4/2 = -2.
So solution is x = -2, y = 5.

Step 4: Find m using y = mx + 3:
5 = m(-2) + 3
5 - 3 = -2m
2 = -2m ⇒ m = -1.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check m = -1:
y = (-1)(-2) + 3 = 2 + 3 = 5 (True)
Boxed Answer: [ x = -2, y = 5, and m = -1 ].
concept_questions: What is the geometrical meaning of finding m in y = mx + 3?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.2 Q3 (iv): The taxi charges in a city consist of a fixed charge together with the charge for the distance covered. For a distance of 10 km, the charge paid is ₹ 105 and for a journey of 15 km, the charge paid is ₹ 155. What are the fixed charges and the charge per km? How much does a person have to pay for travelling a distance of 25 km?
worked_examples.solution:
Let fixed charge = ₹ x, charge per km = ₹ y.
Total charge = Fixed charge + (Distance × Rate per km) = x + d·y.

Case 1 (10 km costs ₹ 105):
x + 10y = 105 ... (1)

Case 2 (15 km costs ₹ 155):
x + 15y = 155 ... (2)

Step 1: From (1), x = 105 - 10y ... (3)

Step 2: Substitute into (2):
(105 - 10y) + 15y = 155
105 + 5y = 155
5y = 50 ⇒ y = ₹ 10 per km.

Step 3: Substitute y = 10 into (3):
x = 105 - 10(10) = 105 - 100 = ₹ 5 (Fixed charge).

Step 4: Cost for travelling 25 km:
Cost = x + 25y = 5 + 25(10) = 5 + 250 = ₹ 255.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check 10 km: 5 + 10(10) = 105
Check 15 km: 5 + 15(10) = 155
25 km: 5 + 250 = 255
Boxed Answer: [ Fixed charge = ₹ 5, Charge per km = ₹ 10. Cost for 25 km = ₹ 255 ].
concept_questions: Why does the difference between the two total costs directly give 5 times the rate per km?
What is the physical meaning of the y-intercept in this linear cost model?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.2 Q3 (vi): Five years hence, the age of Jacob will be three times that of his son. Five years ago, Jacob's age was seven times that of his son. What are their present ages?
worked_examples.solution:
Let Jacob's present age = x years, Son's present age = y years.

Condition 1 (5 years hence / in future):
Jacob's age = x + 5, Son's age = y + 5
Given: (x + 5) = 3(y + 5)
x + 5 = 3y + 15 ⇒ x - 3y = 10 ... (1)

Condition 2 (5 years ago / in past):
Jacob's age = x - 5, Son's age = y - 5
Given: (x - 5) = 7(y - 5)
x - 5 = 7y - 35 ⇒ x - 7y = -30 ... (2)

Step 1: From (1), x = 3y + 10 ... (3)

Step 2: Substitute into (2):
(3y + 10) - 7y = -30
-4y = -40 ⇒ y = 10 years (Son's age).

Step 3: Substitute y = 10 into (3):
x = 3(10) + 10 = 30 + 10 = 40 years (Jacob's age).
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check 5 years hence: Jacob = 45, Son = 15. 45 = 3 × 15 (True)
Check 5 years ago: Jacob = 35, Son = 5. 35 = 7 × 5 (True)
Boxed Answer: [ Jacob's present age = 40 years, Son's present age = 10 years ].
concept_questions: Why must we add 5 to BOTH people's ages when looking 5 years into the future?
Can age ever be negative or fractional in these word problems?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.3 Q2 (iii): The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 9. Also, nine times this number is twice the number obtained by reversing the order of the digits. Find the number.
worked_examples.solution:
Let tens digit = x, units digit = y.
Original Number = 10x + y.
Reversed Number (digits swapped) = 10y + x.

Condition 1: Sum of digits is 9:
x + y = 9 ... (1)

Condition 2: 9 times original number = 2 times reversed number:
9(10x + y) = 2(10y + x)
90x + 9y = 20y + 2x
90x - 2x + 9y - 20y = 0
88x - 11y = 0
Divide entire equation by 11:
8x - y = 0 ... (2)

Step 1: Solve (1) and (2) using Elimination Method.
Add Equation (1) and Equation (2) directly (coefficients of y are +1 and -1):
(x + y) + (8x - y) = 9 + 0
9x = 9 ⇒ x = 1 (Tens digit).

Step 2: Substitute x = 1 into (1):
1 + y = 9 ⇒ y = 8 (Units digit).

Step 3: Construct the original number:
Number = 10x + y = 10(1) + 8 = 18.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check sum of digits: 1 + 8 = 9 (True)
Original = 18, Reversed = 81
9 × 18 = 162
2 × 81 = 162
9 × 18 = 2 × 81 (True!)
Boxed Answer: [ The number is 18 ].
concept_questions: Why is a two-digit number written as 10x + y and NOT xy?
What is the difference between the sum of digits and the value of the number?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.3 Q2 (iv): Meena went to a bank to withdraw ₹ 2000. She asked the cashier to give her ₹ 50 and ₹ 100 notes only. Meena got 25 notes in all. Find how many notes of ₹ 50 and ₹ 100 she received.
worked_examples.solution:
Let number of ₹ 50 notes = x, number of ₹ 100 notes = y.

Condition 1: Total number of notes is 25:
x + y = 25 ... (1)

Condition 2: Total monetary value is ₹ 2000:
50x + 100y = 2000 ... (2)
Divide equation (2) by 50 to simplify:
x + 2y = 40 ... (3)

Step 1: Subtract Equation (1) from Equation (3) using Elimination:
(x + 2y) - (x + y) = 40 - 25
y = 15 (₹ 100 notes).

Step 2: Substitute y = 15 into Equation (1):
x + 15 = 25 ⇒ x = 10 (₹ 50 notes).
[ROUGH_WORK]
Value check:
10 × ₹ 50 = ₹ 500
15 × ₹ 100 = ₹ 1500
Total = ₹ 500 + ₹ 1500 = ₹ 2000 (Matches!)
Total notes = 10 + 15 = 25 (Matches!)
Boxed Answer: [ Meena received 10 notes of ₹ 50 and 15 notes of ₹ 100 ].
concept_questions: Why was dividing equation (2) by 50 such an effective algebraic tactic?

worked_examples.problem: Exercise 3.3 Q2 (v): A lending library has a fixed charge for the first three days and an additional charge for each day thereafter. Saritha paid ₹ 27 for a book kept for seven days, while Susy paid ₹ 21 for the book she kept for five days. Find the fixed charge and the charge for each extra day.
worked_examples.solution:
Let fixed charge for first 3 days = ₹ x.
Let additional charge per day after 3 days = ₹ y.

Case 1 (Saritha kept book for 7 days):
First 3 days cost = x
Extra days = 7 - 3 = 4 days
Total charge = x + 4y = 27 ... (1)

Case 2 (Susy kept book for 5 days):
First 3 days cost = x
Extra days = 5 - 3 = 2 days
Total charge = x + 2y = 21 ... (2)

Step 1: Subtract Equation (2) from Equation (1) using Elimination:
(x + 4y) - (x + 2y) = 27 - 21
2y = 6 ⇒ y = ₹ 3 per extra day.

Step 2: Substitute y = 3 into Equation (2):
x + 2(3) = 21
x + 6 = 21 ⇒ x = ₹ 15 (Fixed charge for first 3 days).
[ROUGH_WORK]
Saritha: 15 + 4(3) = 15 + 12 = 27
Susy: 15 + 2(3) = 15 + 6 = 21
Boxed Answer: [ Fixed charge for first 3 days = ₹ 15, Additional charge per day = ₹ 3 ].
concept_questions: Why did we write 4y instead of 7y for Saritha's equation?
What is the total cost if someone returns the book on the 3rd day?

title: Board Exam Advanced Word Problems: Upstream-Downstream Dynamics & Work-Time Systems
description: Master classic high-weightage Board Exam word problems. Detailed mastery of upstream and downstream relative speeds, reducible linear systems (1/x, 1/y), and combined rate of work problems.
key_concepts: Relative Speed in Water: Speed of boat in still water = x km/h, speed of stream = y km/h
Downstream Speed: (x + y) km/h (stream assists boat)
Upstream Speed: (x - y) km/h (stream opposes boat; requires x > y)
Time Formula: Time = Distance / Speed
Work-Time Invariant: If a person completes work in x days, work done in 1 day = 1/x
Reducible Substitution: Replacing 1/u = p and 1/v = q to linearize equations
subtopics: Classic Boat Problem: 30 km upstream & 44 km downstream in 10 hours
Embroidery Work Problem: 2 women & 5 men in 4 days vs 3 women & 6 men in 3 days
Train and Bus Mixed Journey Problem

worked_examples.problem: Board Exam Classic (NCERT Example 19): A boat goes 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours. In 13 hours, it can go 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream. Determine the speed of the stream and that of the boat in still water.
worked_examples.solution:
Let speed of boat in still water = x km/h.
Let speed of stream = y km/h (where x > y).
Speed upstream = (x - y) km/h.
Speed downstream = (x + y) km/h.
Formula: Time = Distance / Speed.

Case 1 (10 hours total):
Time upstream = 30 / (x - y)
Time downstream = 44 / (x + y)
30 / (x - y) + 44 / (x + y) = 10 ... (1)

Case 2 (13 hours total):
40 / (x - y) + 55 / (x + y) = 13 ... (2)

Step 1: Linearise by substitution:
Let u = 1 / (x - y) and v = 1 / (x + y)
30u + 44v = 10 ... (3)
40u + 55v = 13 ... (4)

Step 2: Solve for u and v using Elimination:
Multiply (3) by 4: 120u + 176v = 40 ... (5)
Multiply (4) by 3: 120u + 165v = 39 ... (6)
Subtract (6) from (5):
(176v - 165v) = 40 - 39
11v = 1 ⇒ v = 1/11.

Step 3: Find u by substituting v = 1/11 into (3):
30u + 44(1/11) = 10
30u + 4 = 10
30u = 6 ⇒ u = 6/30 = 1/5.

Step 4: Solve for x and y:
u = 1/5 ⇒ 1 / (x - y) = 1/5 ⇒ x - y = 5 ... (7)
v = 1/11 ⇒ 1 / (x + y) = 1/11 ⇒ x + y = 11 ... (8)

Add (7) and (8):
2x = 16 ⇒ x = 8 km/h.
Substitute x = 8 into (8):
8 + y = 11 ⇒ y = 3 km/h.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Upstream speed = 8 - 3 = 5 km/h. 30/5 = 6 hours.
Downstream speed = 8 + 3 = 11 km/h. 44/11 = 4 hours.
Total = 6 + 4 = 10 hours. (Verified!)
Case 2: 40/5 + 55/11 = 8 + 5 = 13 hours. (Verified!)
Boxed Answer: [ Speed of boat in still water = 8 km/h, Speed of stream = 3 km/h ].
concept_questions: Why must the boat's speed x be strictly greater than the stream's speed y?
What would happen physically if the speed of the stream exceeded the speed of the boat?

worked_examples.problem: Board Exam Classic: 2 women and 5 men can together finish an embroidery work in 4 days, while 3 women and 6 men can finish it in 3 days. Find the time taken by 1 woman alone to finish the work, and also that taken by 1 man alone.
worked_examples.solution:
Let time taken by 1 woman alone = x days.
Let time taken by 1 man alone = y days.
Work done by 1 woman in 1 day = 1/x.
Work done by 1 man in 1 day = 1/y.

Case 1 (2 women and 5 men finish in 4 days):
Work done in 1 day = 1/4.
2(1/x) + 5(1/y) = 1/4 ... (1)

Case 2 (3 women and 6 men finish in 3 days):
Work done in 1 day = 1/3.
3(1/x) + 6(1/y) = 1/3 ... (2)

Step 1: Substitute u = 1/x and v = 1/y:
2u + 5v = 1/4 ⇒ 8u + 20v = 1 ... (3)
3u + 6v = 1/3 ⇒ 9u + 18v = 1 ... (4)

Step 2: Solve by elimination:
Multiply (3) by 9: 72u + 180v = 9 ... (5)
Multiply (4) by 8: 72u + 144v = 8 ... (6)
Subtract (6) from (5):
36v = 1 ⇒ v = 1/36 ⇒ y = 36 days (Man alone).

Step 3: Substitute v = 1/36 into (3):
8u + 20(1/36) = 1
8u + 5/9 = 1
8u = 4/9 ⇒ u = 4/(9 × 8) = 1/18 ⇒ x = 18 days (Woman alone).
[ROUGH_WORK]
2(1/18) + 5(1/36) = 1/9 + 5/36 = 9/36 = 1/4 (Matches 4 days!)
Boxed Answer: [ Time taken by 1 woman alone = 18 days, Time taken by 1 man alone = 36 days ].
concept_questions: Why do we work with the reciprocal of days (rate of work per day)?
Does 1 woman work twice as fast as 1 man according to this solution?

        <g id="header">
          <text x="24" y="32" fill="#0F172A" font-size="14" font-weight="700" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif">Consistency Criteria & Graphical Geometric Behavior</text>
          <text x="24" y="48" fill="#64748B" font-size="11" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif">Classification matrix linking ratio comparisons to solution multiplicity</text>
        </g>
        
  
    <g transform="translate(40, 70)">
      <rect width="500" height="230" fill="#F8FAFC" stroke="#CBD5E1" stroke-width="1.5" rx="10"/>
      <text x="24" y="28" fill="#0F172A" font-size="13" font-weight="700">Pair of Linear Equations: a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 & a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0</text>
      
      <!-- Row 1: Intersecting -->
      <g transform="translate(16, 42)">
        <rect width="468" height="52" fill="#EFF6FF" stroke="#BFDBFE" rx="6"/>
        <text x="14" y="22" fill="#1E40AF" font-size="12" font-weight="700">1. a₁ / a₂ ≠ b₁ / b₂</text>
        <text x="180" y="22" fill="#0F172A" font-size="11">Intersecting Lines</text>
        <text x="310" y="22" fill="#166534" font-size="11" font-weight="700">Exactly 1 Solution (Unique)</text>
        <text x="14" y="42" fill="#475569" font-size="10">System is Consistent with an independent single point of concurrency</text>
      </g>
      
      <!-- Row 2: Coincident -->
      <g transform="translate(16, 102)">
        <rect width="468" height="52" fill="#F0FDF4" stroke="#BBF7D0" rx="6"/>
        <text x="14" y="22" fill="#166534" font-size="12" font-weight="700">2. a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂</text>
        <text x="180" y="22" fill="#0F172A" font-size="11">Coincident Lines</text>
        <text x="310" y="22" fill="#166534" font-size="11" font-weight="700">Infinitely Many Solutions</text>
        <text x="14" y="42" fill="#475569" font-size="10">System is Consistent (Dependent) where every point on the line is a solution</text>
      </g>
      
      <!-- Row 3: Parallel -->
      <g transform="translate(16, 162)">
        <rect width="468" height="52" fill="#FEF2F2" stroke="#FECACA" rx="6"/>
        <text x="14" y="22" fill="#DC2626" font-size="12" font-weight="700">3. a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ ≠ c₁ / c₂</text>
        <text x="180" y="22" fill="#0F172A" font-size="11">Parallel Lines</text>
        <text x="310" y="22" fill="#DC2626" font-size="11" font-weight="700">No Solution</text>
        <text x="14" y="42" fill="#475569" font-size="10">System is Inconsistent with lines never intersecting in the Euclidean plane</text>
      </g>
    </g>
    
</svg>
